messages:
janet: Cutting RC v4.0.0-rc1 for batching + runtime optimizer. Artifact sha256=fa12be34cafe5678deadbeef0011223344556677. Change window 2026-03-23 03:00-05:00 UTC. Canary plan: kv-warm (t-10m) -> canary 3% (10m) -> 25% (20m) -> 100% gradual. Rollback: promote previous v3.9.8 + flip `runtime_optimizer` flag to false. Release notes: https://go/release-notes/v4.0.0-rc1. Need quick thumbs from infra/telemetry.
deploy-bot: rc created: rc-v4.0.0-rc1 (artifact fa12be34...). Promo window scheduled 2026-03-23T03:00Z. Use `/deploy promote rc-v4.0.0-rc1 --pin=fa12be34cafe` to promote. KV warm dry-run passed in staging.
mario: LGTM. I'll watch the runtime pool and autoscaler during canary. Adding memory/cpu guard: if heap RSS > 80% for 5m, abort and rollback.
deepa: I'll own SLO/trace checks. Also verifying cost delta and rerun the eval suite on canary traffic subset.
rob: quick check: no DB migrations? Any infra toggles?
janet: No migrations. Only runtime config and an updated attention kernel. I added the kernel compatibility matrix to the release notes.
deploy-bot: kv-warm job started at 2026-03-23T02:50Z. Warm progress: 67% -> 92% -> 99% (complete). Cold start baseline unchanged in staging.
oncall-sheriff: ack. I'll be primary pager for the window and monitoring #telemetry and #incidents.
janet: kicking canary now -> 3%
deploy-bot: canary initiated: 3% traffic -> rc-v4.0.0-rc1
deepa: Initial canary: traces ok, p95 down 10ms, error rate slightly down. Nice.
mario: saw a transient CPU spike on one host at t+4m (78% -> 93%), autoscaler added one node and CPU normalized. Noted in the incident log. No customer impact.
rob: runbook note: if autoscaler fails to add capacity within 2m, we abort. Good that it recovered.
deepa: smoke tests passing. Eval suite on canary subset ok.
deploy-bot: scheduled escalation to 25% in 10m unless aborted.
janet: escalation to 25% now. tagging traffic shift.
deploy-bot: canary escalation executed: 25% -> rc-v4.0.0-rc1
mario: Monitoring: no SLO regression, error budget usage stable. CPU at 72% avg, memory stable. One ingestion service reported increased tail latency; digging in.
deepa: the ingestion tail appears tied to a queue consumer backpressure — opened a quick PR to increase consumer concurrency for the ingestion pipeline; patch tested in staging and will be hotpatched if needed.
rob: we should keep the old artifact pinned for rollback. pin recorded: beef00112233 (v3.9.8)
janet: pinned previous artifact and prepared rollback script:

# rollback command
/deploy promote v3.9.8 --pin=beef00112233 --reason="rollback v4.0.0-rc1"
# flip feature flag
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" https://flags.internal/flags/runtime_optimizer/off

deploy-bot: holding at 25% for 20m. Auto-promote to 100% scheduled after hold if no aborts.
oncall-sheriff: No alerts in last 12m. Watching ingestion queue metrics and SLOs.
mario: ingestion consumer hotpatch deployed on a single shard — tail latency back to baseline on that shard. Rolling hotpatch to remaining shards now.
deepa: all shards showing normalized latency. Proceed to full promotion when ready.
janet: promoting to 100% now. executing `/deploy promote rc-v4.0.0-rc1 --pin=fa12be34cafe`
deploy-bot: Promotion complete. Traffic at 100% for rc-v4.0.0-rc1. Old version v3.9.8 pinned for 45m rollback window.
oncall-sheriff: rollback window active (45m). I'll escalate immediately if any SLO violations.
rob: final checks: release note link updated with kernel fallback instructions and metrics offsets. Docs PR: https://go/internal-docs/changes/v4-kernel-fallback
mario: Monitoring cost and infra. Small increase in average token processing throughput but within expected bounds. No action.
deepa: closing evaluation loop: no regressions detected. Will publish GA checklist after rollback window.
janet: thanks team. Filing the post-rollout changelog and will archive this thread after rollback window expires. :tada:
